title: Berger Paints India Ltd - 509480 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Berger Paints Q2 FY27 standalone revenue grew 11.9% on ~8% decorative price growth, but standalone PBDIT fell 4.4% and PAT 7.3% as gross margin compressed.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 11.9% in Q2 FY27 and 12.3% in H1, with volume up 3% in Q2 and 5.6% in H1, per management. Gross margin fell to 36.6% in Q2 (38.1% in H1) as double-digit raw material inflation, liquidation of high-cost inventory and delayed industrial price hikes hit margins. Q2 EBITDA margin was 10.8% (standalone), and H1 was 14.4%, below management's 15-17% guided range; a Rs 22 crore extra spend on the new Rangbanara Rahe campaign weighed on the quarter. Consolidated revenue grew 13.2% in Q2 and PBDIT 5.2%, with subsidiaries strong and the JVs (Berger Becker, BNPA) contributing; management expects Q3 and Q4 margins to recover toward the guided band.

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Double-digit value growth driven by about 8% price growth; volumes moderated as later Diwali shifted demand to Q3 and price-sensitive putty, textures and enamel de-grew. Home sealing products (roof coat, Dam Shield) and wood coatings grew strongly.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: High double-digit volume and value growth across automotive (about 5-6% of mix, growing about 31% on two-wheeler demand), protective and general industrial; gross margin fell about 5.5% as price hikes lagged raw material inflation.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Bolik's SA grew strongly; BJ and Nepal showed robust revenue and profit growth; STP revenue and operating profit grew well with margins moderating; SBL growth on pricing with profitability hit by solvent RM inflation; Berger Becker coil coatings and BNPA grew over 40% in revenue, with margins compressed (JVs contribute only 49% of profit).

guidance_outlook: Management is confident EBITDA margin will get close to the 15-17% band in Q3 and possibly Q4, supported by calibrated price increases, cost-saving initiatives and cost discipline.
Industrial price hikes: about 90% of targeted increase expected to be recovered by end-November, the balance by December.
Raw material prices (largely crude-linked) softened slightly in Q2 and that drop is expected to carry into Q3; management did not give a fixed view on month-to-month movement.
October was the highest monthly sales growth in about 25-30 months; management expects strong revenue growth in Q3 on festive demand.
Working capital to normalise as input costs stabilise; company intends to remain net cash.
Urban-market experiment (MEGA framework) to be finalised by March 2027, with acceleration from April 2027.
capex_capacity: Hindustan (Kolkata-area) plant expansion just completed, per management.
West Bengal government announced a new industrial incentive policy; company to evaluate investment scale for its Panagarh plant.
Plans for a new factory in Orissa; both new factories to be funded from internal cash rather than borrowing, with short-term borrowing possible.
Capex in new factories expected at a later date; no quantified amount given.
demand_pricing: Decorative price growth of about 8%; new entrant previously priced about 5% below industry and has now moved to industry parity but is rebating more to dealers, so competitive intensity remains.
Market share (top-6 listed companies basis) about 20.2% at H1 vs 20.3% earlier: stable, no loss or gain in the half.
Urban markets: Berger has under half its all-India share there (e.g. about 7-8% in Bangalore, lower in Pune and Mumbai), seen as a major opportunity.
Industrial price increases partly passed on; some rebates pulled back in certain decorative categories, which restrained top-line growth.
Retail store network of 2,000+ stores and tinting and point-of-sale expansion continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the receivables and inventory build-up in the cash flow statement, and will gross margin recovery take time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory rose by about Rs 400 crore as a planned build ahead of the big October festive sales, at peak raw material prices. Gross margin outlook was not guided precisely given volatile RM prices; there is a lag between consumption and COGS.

qa_highlights.question: Will Asian Paints' backward integration into VAM/VAE and possible price cuts affect Berger's competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has its own cost-efficiency plans and will see the quantum of any savings before deciding how to respond; it expects visible gross and EBITDA margin improvement from its own measures.

qa_highlights.question: How is the marketing spend expected to behave, given past campaigns?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand building needs sustained spend; the Rangbanara Rahe corporate campaign is the first in many years. Spend will taper after launch, with bursts roughly every 7-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Status of urban-penetration strategy, moving from walls to space, and use of free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Urban experiment is yielding positive results and will be finalised by March 2027, then accelerated from April 2027. Berger will stay in paints, coatings, construction chemicals and waterproofing; surplus cash to fund West Bengal and Orissa factories, not borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and market share trend in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share about 20.2% vs 20.3% earlier, relatively stable. Management said it aims to hold share, not to gain heavily, given intense competition.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases have been pushed in industrial and the gross margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial gross margin fell about 5.5%; October price increases taken, with 90% of target expected by end-November and the rest by December. Recovery depends on crude staying at lower levels.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on crude-linked raw material prices, which are volatile; a rebound would erode the planned industrial price recovery.

Competitive intensity from the new entrant, which is rebating more to dealers after raising list prices; a possible backward-integrated cost advantage from a rival (VAM plant) was raised by an analyst.
Q2 receivables and inventory build-up (inventory up about Rs 400 crore) needs to unwind in Q3.
Marketing spend ramp for the new campaign may keep A&P elevated and weigh on margins in coming quarters.
Decorative volumes slowed in price-sensitive categories (putty, textures, enamel); volume growth was only 3% in Q2.
Sales-return ratio query raised by an analyst was not resolved on the call; to be followed up with IR.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the Q3 festive run-rate, but defensive on margins: management attributed the Q2 squeeze to RM inflation, price-hike lag and campaign spend. It was evasive on the timing of gross margin recovery and on competitor cost moves, and it dismissed a question on share price.
key_quotes: We are quite confident that we will be quite close to that 15% to 17% band that we have indicated.
Our guided range is 15 to 17, so at the end of half-year, we are at 14.4, which is close to that.
October was the month when we had the highest, you know, sales growth in the last possibly 25, 30 months.
We have no desire to diversify into other areas.

growth.why: Standalone revenue grew 11.9% in Q2 (volume +3%, ~8% decorative price) and management expects EBITDA margin to approach the 15-17% band in Q3/Q4 via price hikes (90% of industrial hikes recovered by end-Nov), cost actions and softer crude-linked RM, with October the strongest sales month in 25-30 months; no revenue growth figure guided and no quantified capacity added, so backing is partial.
